# T289 — erase(live opening) slates; the drop is the cut; lifecycle under the container

Working spec: `.adlc/specs/64-slated-opening-until-drop.md`. Read it first; it carries the user stories, Myk's rulings of 2026-09-08 and the correction of 2026-09-09, the contract, and the acceptance criteria with their verification paths. This ticket stacks on T288 (#566). PR #567's cleanup vocabulary is superseded and must not merge.

## What to build

1. `Gateway.erase(openingId)` on a protected `open` event whose pool is attached (a pool whose `declarationId` equals the opening's `poolDeclaration`) purges nothing. Under `withChannelCommit`, it writes a §29 slate over that incarnation (opening, receipts, close, pinned by address) and refuses with a message that names the pool container that must be dropped and says the pool can still be read or extracted. While slated: `sync` refuses, reads of the pool work, a second erase and a fresh same-name open refuse and name the slate.
2. `dropChannel` on a slated channel is the cut: the existing byte-verified pool purge and detach, then marked tombstones for the opening, its receipts and its close, then the slate is retired as §29.5 retires a cut slate. A refused purge leaves the slate standing and erases nothing.
3. `Gateway.erase(openingId)` on an opening whose pool is not attached erases that incarnation's opening, receipts and close directly, with marked tombstones naming the channel and the pool declaration. It touches no pool. A later incarnation of the same name is unaffected.
4. Every protected lifecycle event carries an entity pointer at the parent container: role `into`, context `loam.local.channel.event`, id = the `into` container name. Never role `container` at `loam.container`. A bound connection's lineage read filters by it; the operator's read may filter by it. One pointer, at `into`, never per ancestor.
5. Remove T288's outright erase of a live opening and its `erased opening` refusal of `drop`.

## Acceptance criteria

The spec's criteria 1–10 are the rail list. Two rail files: `test/federation/local-channel-slated-opening.test.ts` (criteria 1–5) and `test/federation/local-channel-container-scope.test.ts` (criteria 6–7). Every purging case asserts a named live bystander at the bytes. Each rail file records its rails-red run on the #566 tip and its revert probes in its header. The two T288 cases named under Migration are revised in the same stack or through the authorized revision road. Declare `rails` on this ticket only when the files exist.

Verify: `npx vitest run test/federation/local-channel-slated-opening.test.ts test/federation/local-channel-container-scope.test.ts`, then `npm run check`, then `adlc hollow-test --base origin/t288/local-channel-events --max 300 --test-cmd "timeout -k 10 600 npx vitest run test/federation/local-channel-*.test.ts"` on the clean tip before any evidence is recorded.

## Merge

This narrows what erase can purge on its own: a live opening is never purged by erase, only by the operator's drop. Myk merges, because it changes what the erase door promises.
title: Erasing a live channel opening slates it until the drop; lifecycle events file under the parent container
